newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans to convert pension debts into bonds.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans to convert pension debts into bonds.

text.p: Russia plans to convert company and state debt to pensioners into bonds, Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Sysuyev said on Wednesday.
"We have such plans regarding debts to the Pension Fund," Sysuyev told a news conference. "But this is not an easy problem."
He said the government had to make sure bond plans tallied with existing legislation before launching the programme.
He also said the government feared companies would think their debts were forgotten the moment the government started restructuring the debt.
Companies have to transfer funds to the state Pension Fund, which accumulates money to be paid out to pensioners, on a monthly basis.

Pension Fund Debt Repayment Department Head Valentina Konstantinova told Reuters that on April 1, 1997, the volume of debt to the fund amounted to 69 trillion roubles ($12 billion), up from January 1 of 15.7 trillion roubles.
The state plans to pay all pension arrears by July 1, but Sysuyev declined to say how much of the debt the government had already paid.
The debt will be paid out of the government's sources, including proceeds from operations on international markets, he said.
Russia has recently placed its $2 billion Eurobond and a senior Finance Ministry official said the revenues would go to cover the budget deficit.
The social debt represents company and government debts to municipal employees, the military and pensioners.

The government has already converted farmers' debt to the state into one, two and three-year bonds. The first auction took place last week and the government plans to launch secondary trading in the paper soon.
